extraction_scope: Worker-6 final mechanism ontology record after source review of XML/PDF/OA figures; automated membrane/nucleic-acid placeholder claims were replaced with PEDV entry/fusion and neutralization evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: HR2-derived peptides inhibit PEDV infection primarily in entry/co-treatment assays, supporting a functional entry-inhibition mechanism rather than a membrane-disruption or nucleic-acid mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PEDV HR2M, HR2L, and HR2P peptides against PEDV-GFP in Huh7 cells

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=3:Fig. 3; xml:fig=4:Fig. 4; xml:sec=16:PEDV HR2-derived peptides exhibited antiviral activity in vitro; xml:sec=17:HR2L and HR2P have potent antiviral activities at different steps of viral infection and cross-reacted with G1 PEDV

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper did not resolve a crystal structure and did not directly show peptide-HR1 binding; the mechanism is framed as source-supported functional entry/fusion inhibition.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Anti-HR2P polyclonal antiserum neutralizes PEDV-GFP in vitro, consistent with HR2P mimicking a neutralizing epitope of PEDV.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: mouse anti-HR2P antiserum against PEDV-GFP in Huh7 cells

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=6:Fig. 6; xml:sec=18:Neutralizing activity of the polyclonal antisera against HR2P

mechanism_claims.limitations: Neutralization is shown in vitro; no in vivo protection or clinical efficacy claim is made.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The HR1/HR2 six-helix bundle fusion-core model is used as mechanistic context for PEDV S2-mediated membrane fusion, but the paper reports unsuccessful crystal-structure determination.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=1:Fig. 1; xml:sec=14:Organization of the HR regions in the PEDV S glycoprotein; xml:sec=20:Discussion

mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote to direct structural binding evidence; it remains a model-backed interpretation plus functional assay context.
